the Mediterranean diet is associated with a reduction in the incidence of CVD.
a high-fat, plant-based MeDiet is associated with reduced risk of CVD.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a MeDiet, supplemented with nuts or EVOO, reduces CVD events and diabetes incidence, improves the metabolic profile, and has a beneficial effect on the expression of genes involved in vascular and metabolic events.
the MeDiet, with or without EVOO or nuts, is a healthy dietary pattern that may reduce CVD risk and the incidence of type 2 diabetes in high-risk individuals.
the MeDiet, which includes high intake of fruits and vegetables and low intake of red meat, is associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome.
